concerns.text: The three Edge Cases specify required system behaviors (redshift-gap masking with warning, graceful empty-candidate handling returning p-value 1.0, automatic downsample to nside=32 on memory pressure) but no FR covers any of them. FR-001–FR-006 are all anchored to US-1/2/3 acceptance scenarios only. Add FRs (e.g. FR-007–FR-009) covering these edge-case behaviors, or fold them into existing FRs, so they are buildable and testable.

Edge case says 'The system must automatically downsample to nside=32 and log the resolution change', but Constitution Principle VII mandates 'consistent HEALPix pixelization (nside = 64) across both the Planck 2018 temperature maps and the SDSS/DES galaxy density shells' for ALL cross-correlation analyses, and FR-001/US-1 fix nside=64. A nside=32 fallback would violate the constitution and break grid consistency with the galaxy maps. Specify a fallback that preserves nside=64 (e.g., restrict sky fraction per the Assumptions section) or reconcile explicitly.

'outputs a list of 10–50 candidate cold spot coordinates' pre-asserts an empirical count, while the Success Criteria section states planning docs defer 'counts, dataset sizes, measured quantities' via [deferred] (as done in US-1 and US-2 scenario 2). Replace the 10–50 range with a [deferred] count or a stated measurement reference for consistency with the document's own deferral convention.

FR-006 requires ALL computations (data loading, correlation, simulation) to complete within 6 hours but is tagged 'serving US-1 (See US-1)' only, while US-3's scenario separately imposes 'p-value within 60 seconds of simulation completion'. The 6-hour budget spans US-1/2/3; the story anchor understates its scope. Re-anchor to US-1/US-2/US-3 or state it is a project-wide constraint.

"outputs a list of 10–50 candidate cold spot coordinates" hard-codes an empirical outcome on real Planck data. The actual count at −2σ/5° is unknown a priori; if reality yields 8 or 60 spots the criterion fails despite a correct implementation. Restate as a checkable property (e.g., non-empty list of coordinates each satisfying the threshold), deferring the count.

"automatically downsample to nside=32" conflicts with Constitution Principle VII, which mandates nside=64 consistency for all cross-correlation analyses. A nside=32 fallback is either untestable end-to-end (results would violate the constitution) or must be scoped as a preprocessing-only fallback with correlation recomputed at nside=64. Also specify how the memory-failure path is exercised (e.g., unit fixture on a synthetic oversized map), since it cannot be reliably triggered on the real dataset.

"measured against the theoretical prediction of the Integrated Sachs-Wolfe effect" names no concrete reference — which prediction (ISW ΔT amplitude formula, which supervoid profile/parameters)? As written, an implementer cannot know what to compare the alignment strength against. Name the theoretical quantity and its source.

Under-reach: the idea's methodology sketch requires 'convergence plots showing correlation significance as a function of redshift bin AND cold spot threshold'. The spec covers threshold sensitivity (FR-005, SC-002) but nowhere requires reporting significance per redshift bin (z=0.2–1.0) or a plot of significance vs. redshift bin. Add an FR/SC for per-bin significance reporting.

Under-reach (minor): the idea lists final outputs as 'correlation plots, p-value table, and reproducible Jupyter notebook'. The spec covers the p-value table (FR-005) but does not state the deliverable form of the correlation plots or the reproducible notebook. Clarify the output artifacts so the deliverable scope matches the idea.

A Kolmogorov-Smirnov test is a two-sample (or one-sample vs CDF) distribution comparison. Here there is ONE observed correlation amplitude (a scalar) vs 1000 simulated amplitudes. Applying a KS test to a single observed value is a statistical category error; the correct test is a one-sided tail probability from the Monte Carlo null (rank of the observed amplitude within the 1000 realizations). FR-004 and US-3 SC-1 must be reworded to specify the MC rank/tail-probability test (or a z-score against the null distribution), not a KS test.

The null construction is underspecified in a way that could invalidate significance: if the 1000 ΛCDM realizations are pure Gaussian CMB skies, the null omits the galaxy map's shot noise, photometric-redshift scatter, and survey mask/geometry. The null must be generated by applying the SAME cold-spot detection + cross-correlation pipeline to simulated skies while keeping the actual (masked) galaxy density maps fixed, otherwise the p-value does not test the alignment claim. Spec should state that realizations pass through the identical pipeline and survey mask.

The sensitivity sweep {-2.0σ, -2.05σ, -2.1σ} spans a 0.1σ range — so narrow that p-value stability across it is nearly guaranteed by construction and cannot demonstrate threshold robustness. A meaningful robustness check needs a wider sweep (e.g. -1.5σ to -3σ in 0.25σ steps) or variation of the filter radius too.

SC-004 says alignment strength is 'measured against the theoretical prediction of the ISW effect for supervoids' but no FR computes a theoretical ISW template/amplitude (e.g. from a ΛCDM linear-theory cross-correlation or a supervoid profile model). Either add an FR computing the theoretical ISW cross-correlation curve, or reword SC-004 to a qualitative consistency comparison so the criterion is measurable.

The synthetic-Gaussian-field test verifies ξ(θ)≈0 on uncorrelated fields — a useful sanity check, but it cannot validate the detection pipeline's sensitivity. Consider also requiring a synthetic field with a KNOWN injected correlation (positive control) so the pipeline's ability to recover a signal is tested; otherwise the validation only confirms the null case.

new_concerns.text: FRs and edge cases reference user‑story identifiers US-1, US-2, US-3 (e.g., FR‑001 ‘(See US‑1)’, FR‑006 ‘(See US‑1, US‑2, US‑3)’), but the specification only names the stories as “User Story 1”, “User Story 2”, “User Story 3” without assigning those IDs. Define US‑1, US‑2, US‑3 identifiers for the three user stories or adjust the FR anchors to match the existing naming.

The idea explicitly calls for a Kolmogorov‑Smirnov (KS) test to compare the observed cross‑correlation amplitude distribution against the ΛCDM simulations. The spec instead describes a Monte‑Carlo rank‑test p‑value (FR‑004) without justification. Add the KS test as specified, or provide a clear methodological justification for substituting the rank‑test.
